create-entry.name: Create-entry action
create-entry.acceptance: Delivered 2026-10-11: an entry step `op: "create"` (entry_type slug, title, data, metadata, status inbox|draft) makes a schema-validated entry, returns entry_id/slug, sends entry_created at depth+1, previews in a dry run, and makes it once per event (key: correlation id + workflow + target + step, kept in metadata.automation_created).

custom-operation.name: Free-form AI operation
custom-operation.acceptance: Delivered 2026-10-11: an operation step `op: "custom"` carries its own prompt (${…} templates) and output_schema (a JSON Schema object); `see` adds the item, its attachments, images, the workspace persona; the answer is checked (one retry) and is the step output; write_back maps it onto the entry (summary, tags, metadata.<key>), asset or resource; budget, approval mode and min_role apply as for built-in operations. Named, reusable workspace operations are a later phase.

branches.name: Conditional steps (if/else)
branches.acceptance: Delivered 2026-10-11: any step takes `when` conditions evaluated against steps.* / previous.* (same operators); false records it as skipped (not failed), later references read None, and the dry run shows the verdicts.

iterate-aggregate.name: Iterate / aggregate over a target set
iterate-aggregate.acceptance: Delivered 2026-10-12: a `collect` step ("Gather items") runs an entry/asset/resource query (a target's keys) and returns rows (each as ${entry.*}/${asset.*}/${resource.*}), count, total and text (a plain list for an AI prompt), up to the target cap; a render step's list images take the rows whole (grid, moodboard). Linked items (2026-10-12): `entries` (the entry a field names), `asset` / `resource` (the entries using one), an asset/resource query's `entry` (what an entry holds, in its order) and `role`, and sort by `position` (a collection's own order). Delivered 2026-10-13 (0e7c993b): a `repeat` step runs 1–5 inner steps (an AI step included) once per item of a list or a collect step's rows, keyed per item so a re-delivered event repeats nothing; at most 25 items, no wait/approval/repeat inside. Nothing left.

relative-dates.name: Relative dates and cron schedules
relative-dates.acceptance: Delivered 2026-10-12: every date key of a query (created/updated/published_after|before) takes a relative date (-7d, -12h, -2w, +3d, now, today), read when the run starts; an unreadable date fails the query instead of widening it. Cron schedules compute next_run_at in their time zone and fire (services/cron.py).

asset-resource-targets.name: Assets and resources as workflow subjects
asset-resource-targets.acceptance: Delivered (2026-10-08/11): asset_*/resource_* events bind `asset.*` / `resource.*`; targets take entity asset|resource; an operation step on an asset sees its image and writes back through a `write_back` field map. Delivered 2026-10-12: the entries linked to a given asset or resource (`asset` / `resource` query keys). Delivered 2026-10-12: `checksum` (and `exclude`) in an asset query; `asset.checksum` in a run. Derived-asset lineage is part of media-adapters.

workflow-approvals.name: Approval step inside a workflow
workflow-approvals.acceptance: Delivered 2026-10-11: an `approval` step parks the run (snapshot in workflow_approvals), asks members at its role (push, Automation → Approvals, app badge), resumes from the next step with ${steps.<id>.output.decision} (approved | denied | expired | stale — the entry changed after it was asked), expires hourly, and lets integration actions marked requires_approval run in an approved run. Also delivered: one-tap Approve/Deny on the push when every later step can be undone in Marvin (2026-10-11, befe2ef0); `choices` (the approver picks one: `choice`, `choice_index`), length conditions, cancelling a waiting run (2026-10-13, f12b80c1); `image` shown with the question, and a picture's decision stamped on its asset (2026-10-13, 68d8392a / 6c99c7f4); the wait limit is a workspace setting (2026-10-14, 70ac6143).

waits.name: Durable waits and delays
waits.acceptance: Delivered 2026-10-13: a `wait` step — `for` (30m, 12h, 3d, 2w) or `until` a date/datetime with `offset` and `at`, in the workspace's time zone, calendar arithmetic across clock changes — parks the run (workflow_waits, the run's snapshot incl. its inputs); a minutely sweep resumes it with the entry as it is then; the entry in the Trash or the workflow switched off/changed cancels it; a moment already past goes on at once (late); a year at most.

idempotency.name: Per-step idempotency keys
idempotency.acceptance: Delivered 2026-10-18: a webhook or integration step with a templated `idempotency_key` that already made that call (same workflow, same destination, same key) within `idempotency_window_hours` (default 24, 1–720) is skipped and its recorded output reused, marked `idempotency: {duplicate: true}`; two concurrent duplicates deliver once (the first claims the key before it calls); a failed call gives the key back so retries still make it; a dry run says `would: call` or `would: skip (duplicate)`. Kept in `workflow_step_idempotency` as a hash; the Prune Workflow Runs task drops ended windows. It dedupes identical calls: it does not coalesce different keys.

media-adapters.name: Image, file and audio processing adapters
media-adapters.acceptance: Slice 3 delivered 2026-10-12: media ops extract_text (a PDF's text layer; scanned pages and pictures by the vision model, image.read_text), pages (PDF pages as pictures, pypdfium2), find_sensitive and redact (faces, plates, personal text by the vision model, pixelated in a new copy). Slice 2 delivered 2026-10-12: a media step's render op fills an HTML/CSS template (built-in: card, quote, poster, trading-card, meme, side-by-side, comic-4, newspaper — or the step's own html) with text and pictures and screenshots it with headless Chromium into a new asset with lineage; the page runs no script and reaches no network. Slice 1 delivered 2026-10-12: a `media` step (resize, crop with subject focus, convert, grade, inspect, palette) saves NEW assets with lineage (derived_from, derivation, workflow, step, correlation id), never modifies originals, reuses an identical derivation, and attach_as links them to the run's entry; an integration action with an image.* capability keeps its images as assets (generated_by, prompt, model) so runs carry references. Also 2026-10-12: zip (files + manifest.json) and printed renders (format pdf; the guide template). Provider edits 2026-10-12: an integration step's `source` hands an image.edit action the picture (image_b64) and keeps the result as a version of it; OpenAI Images v0.3.0 has `edit`. Left: TTS.

fetch.name: HTTP fetch step
fetch.acceptance: Delivered 2026-10-12: a `fetch` step ("Check a web address") — `url`: GET/HEAD through the guarded client (public hosts, re-checked on redirects, 2 MB cap) → status, ok, content_type, title, text, json, and `find` phrases (any case) → found; `links`: the links in a text checked a few at a time → checked, broken, broken_count, text. A dead link is output, never a failed step; a dry run doesn't fetch.

social-adapters.name: Social publishing adapters
social-adapters.acceptance: Publishing delivered 2026-10-19: the social.post capability (text, images, alt, link, dry_run → posted, post_id, url, network), always behind an Approval step, an integration step with no `integration` posts to every connected network, `per_network` overrides the arguments for one, and a library asset becomes its public URL; each network is its own plugin (Instagram, Facebook Page, Bluesky, Mastodon). Left: drafts and polls as a provider action (poll-companion) and metrics actions that collect numbers from a network (campaign-scoreboard) — no plugin offers either yet.

comments.name: Comment events
comments.acceptance: comment_added/updated/deleted have an emitter that carries entry_id and the comment text, are triggerable, and hydrate `entry.*`.

collection-scope.name: Collection-scoped steps
collection-scope.acceptance: A step can read a collection's entries (`${collection.entries}`) and an operation can run over that set to produce one output (summary, roundup). Partly delivered 2026-10-12: a `collect` step reads a collection's entries in its own order (`collection` + sort `position`) for one step to use; with an AI or `repeat` step over its rows, that is the roundup (2026-10-12/13); left only: `${collection.entries}` bound directly on collection events (a `collect` step reads the same set today).

member-email.name: Member-addressed email
member-email.acceptance: Delivered 2026-10-18: an `email` step ("Email a member") — `to` a member's user id or email (${member.id}, ${member.email}, an entry field), `subject` and `body` (templates; markdown, set in the workspace's email layout and sent through its SMTP profile), optional `heading`, `button_text` + `button_link`, `once_per`. The recipient must be a member of the workspace — an outside address, a member of another workspace only, or a word fails the step, nothing is mailed. Sent once: the same event handled twice, a retry or a re-run sends nothing more (a ledger, `workflow_email_sends`; a failed send gives its claim back); `once_per: welcome:${member.id}` sends that person the step's email once, ever. The step needs an admin author, and fails with no SMTP; a dry run renders the email (would_send) and sends nothing. Role-appropriate links: a `when` on ${member.role}, `${site.url}` (the site) and `${site.app_url}` (the admin app). Left: writing to an address that isn't a member's (a fixed outside recipient stays an email subscription's `specific` recipient), and member_added still carries no email for subscriptions.

custom-events.name: Custom emit_event names
custom-events.acceptance: Delivered 2026-10-18: a workspace registers `custom.<name>` events (Settings → Automation → Custom events, PUT /api/groups/custom-events/{name}) with typed payload fields (string, number, boolean, date); an Emit event step sends one with a templated `payload` held to those fields; a workflow can start on it, webhook/email/integration subscriptions can name it, the editor, Events pages, describe_event and the authoring guide list it; each hop carries reaction_depth + 1, so a chain stops at MAX_REACTION_DEPTH.

ops-triggers.name: Operational events as workflow triggers
ops-triggers.acceptance: Delivered 2026-10-18: ai_budget_threshold_reached/_exceeded, integration_attention_needed/_resolved, webhook_delivery_failed and scheduled_task_failed (the workspace's own tasks; a platform task belongs to no workspace) are triggerable under the editor's Operations heading, their payload fields read as `${event.<field>}` (describe_event and the authoring guide list them). A workflow is never woken by a failure its own run caused: the engine's running-workflow guard covers what a run does itself, and a failed delivery that runs after the run joins the delivered event's chain (correlation id, reaction depth), where a workflow with a run in it sits out. The independent fallback is Settings → Automation → Notifications, which needs no workflow.

joins.name: Parallel branches and joins
joins.acceptance: Delivered 2026-10-18: a `parallel` step ("Parallel branches") runs 2–5 named branches of 1–5 steps (no wait, approval, repeat or parallel inside) one after another in the order written, each reading what ran before it but not its siblings; `join` all (default) or any (the first branch to succeed wins, the rest are skipped); `on_branch_failure` fail (the step fails when the join isn't met; under all the first failing branch stops the rest) or continue (the step reports `satisfied`, `failed`, `text` and each branch's status for a `when`). The merge is by name in written order (`branches.<name>` {status ok|failed|skipped, error, steps, output}, `order`), so it never depends on which branch finished first; branches' steps are keyed per branch so a create inside runs once per event and count against the workspace's steps-per-workflow limit; a dry run previews every branch. Branches run in-process, not concurrently.

snapshots.name: Entity snapshots and restore
snapshots.acceptance: Delivered 2026-10-18: a `snapshot` step captures an entry's title, summary, description, data, metadata, status, collections and attached asset references into `entry_snapshots` (reusing the latest when identical; 20 kept per entry) and a later `restore` step (or `POST /entries/{id}/snapshots/{id}/restore`) puts content, collections and assets back through the entry service, so the normal events fire; status only when asked, through the publish gate, never into or out of the Trash; AUTHOR+ like any entry write; a dry run previews the diff. External publications (a newsletter sent, a webhook delivered) are not restorable and the entry page has no snapshots list yet.

sandbox.name: Schema validation / sandbox handler
sandbox.acceptance: Delivered 2026-10-18: a `schema_check` step ("Check against a schema") — `document` (usually a fetch step's `${steps.<id>.output.json}`, or any template; text holding a JSON object or array is read as JSON) against `schema` (inline, or a template giving one) or `schema_resource` (a resource whose metadata.schema holds it), Draft 2020-12 → valid, errors [{path, message}] (max_errors, default 20, at most 50), error_count, truncated, text. A document that doesn't fit is output, never a failed step, unless `fail_on_invalid`; a malformed inline schema is refused when the workflow is saved; documents over 100 KB are reported, not checked; a dry run checks when it has a document. Left: running anything (a sandbox proper) and graph checks beyond a schema (reachability over cycles).

form-classification.name: Form-submission classification from workflows
form-classification.acceptance: Delivered 2026-10-18: a run on a form submission — a form_submission_received event, or any event on an entry of a submittable type — binds `${form_submission.*}` (id, form, form_slug, data.<field>, status, submitted_at, flagged, review_reasons: the entry the public form saved, or a legacy Forms row), and an operation step with op classify-form-submission reads it by itself (entity_type and entity_id default to the run's submission). Its answer — category, confidence, is_spam, sentiment, tags, action_required — is `${steps.<id>.output.<key>}` for a `when` or a template; a dry run previews with a stand-in answer and asks no AI. describe_event and the authoring guide list the fields.

data-change-detection.name: Data-field change detection
data-change-detection.acceptance: Delivered 2026-10-18: entry_updated (and the publish, unpublish, archive, trash and restore events) name every changed field of the entry's type as `data.<key>` in `changed_fields`, with `before.data.<key>` / `after.data.<key>`; `changed`, `changed_from`, `changed_to` and `${event.before.data.price}` read them. Bounded, not opt-in: a short scalar (≤ 160 characters) is carried by value, a long text (a body), list, object or secret-like field name reads `‹elided›` — still named, so “the body changed” works; 100 names and 25 values per event.

manual-params.name: Manual / MCP run parameters
manual-params.acceptance: Delivered 2026-10-12: a manual trigger's `inputs` (name, label, type text | number | choice | entry, options, required, default) — asked by the Run button's form, passed in the run API's body or run_workflow's `inputs`, checked against the declarations, read as ${input.<name>}; an entry input is the entry the run acts on.

metrics.name: Metrics windows and experiments
metrics.acceptance: Delivered 2026-10-18: a `metric` step ("Record a metric") records a number against a `metric` (slug), optional `variant` and `subject`, and a `window` — day, week (ISO) or month in the workspace's time zone, or one named outright (2026-10-18, 2026-W42, 2026-10); one observation per key, so recording again replaces the value and a rerun never double-counts. `op: "read"` lists observations back (rows, count, total, text headed "Observations, not conclusions:"). A dry run writes nothing. Settings → Automation → Metrics and GET /api/groups/metrics/observations list them (filters: metric, variant, subject, window range); an admin can remove one. No comparison or significance is computed, and no scheduled task trims them. Left: collecting the numbers from a network (social-adapters).

It runs only while the Social engagement task is enabled, and never for the account's own comments (so a reply it sends can't start it again).

recipes.title: An agent drafts from a published entry
recipes.outcome: When an entry of your chosen type is published, an agent does a job from it, such as drafting social posts. The agent uses its own permissions and Playbooks, plus any you add. What it writes lands as drafts in the Inbox.

setup_variables.name: entry_type
setup_variables.description: The entry type that starts the agent when one is published.

setup_variables.name: agent
setup_variables.description: The agent that does the job (Settings → AI → Agents). It needs permission to save drafts: set Entries: author to Allow.

setup_variables.name: message
setup_variables.description: The job, in a sentence or two. The entry's title and link are added for you, along with a reminder to write the text itself and save it as a draft.
setup_variables.example: Draft a Bluesky post and a Mastodon post announcing it, each as its own draft.

setup_variables.name: playbooks
setup_variables.description: Published Playbooks to load in full for this job, on top of the agent's own (up to 3). Leave empty for none.

features: AI available for workflows
An agent that may save drafts: Entries: author set to Allow for it

side_effects.description: Runs the agent once for each publication. This makes several AI calls and uses your monthly AI budget.
Saves drafts to the Inbox for review. Nothing is published.

recipes.cost_notes: Several AI calls per run (one per tool step, at most the step's max_steps), from the workspace's monthly AI budget; the run's tokens and cost show on the run.
recipes.failure_behaviour: An unknown or switched-off agent, a missing Playbook or an over-budget workspace fails the step before the agent runs; the run is recorded and the `workflow_failed` alert fires (if enabled). The agent's drafts are never published, and the step does not run for an event this same workflow caused.
notes: Only the tools the agent's permission matrix sets to Allow are offered: Ask-first tools aren't, so give the agent Entries: author → Allow.
The message tells the agent to write the text itself and save it with create_draft: compose_entry and revise_entry use Marvin's own AI, which never loads Playbooks.
Put an Approval step after the agent step to gate anything that goes public.

recipes.title: An agent reviews the week's changes
recipes.outcome: Every Monday an agent reviews entries of your chosen type that changed in the last 7 days, using its Playbooks. Its answer is kept as the run's result and the findings it drafts land in the Inbox.

trigger.note: A schedule trigger creates its own backing scheduled task (no separate object); interval, cron (in its time zone) and once all run.

setup_variables.name: agent
setup_variables.description: The agent that does the review (Settings → AI → Agents). It needs permission to save drafts: set Entries: author to Allow.

setup_variables.name: entry_type
setup_variables.description: The entry type to review. Only published entries changed in the last 7 days are included.

setup_variables.name: message
setup_variables.description: What to check for. The week's changed entries are added for you, along with a reminder to write each note itself and save it as a draft.
setup_variables.example: Review them for typos, broken promises in the summary, and anything that breaks the house style.

setup_variables.name: timezone
setup_variables.description: The time zone the schedule runs in, for example `America/New_York`.

features: AI available for workflows
An agent that may save drafts: Entries: author set to Allow for it

side_effects.description: Runs the agent each week. This makes several AI calls and uses your monthly AI budget.
Saves drafts to the Inbox for review. Nothing is published.

recipes.cost_notes: One agent run per week (several AI calls, at most the step's max_steps), from the workspace's monthly AI budget; skipped in a week when nothing changed.
recipes.failure_behaviour: An unknown or switched-off agent or an over-budget workspace fails the run before the agent starts; the run is recorded and the `workflow_failed` alert fires (if enabled).
